Four Party A senators defected to support the Party B side, including Person U2 and Person V2 of Region Z, Person Z of Region J, and Person W2 of Region A2. Within 7 days of the cutoff, the media found out that Region I, a small company selling umbrellas and raincoats, had its tariffs soared from 10% to 145% and then fell back again. After the boss was forced to repeatedly change prices and lay off employees, would the public opinion lament that 'it calls for tariffs every day and makes Country X pay, but in the end it is its own small businesses and consumers who foot the bill'?

Within 7 days of the cutoff, on the day of the hearing of the highest judicial body, even the justice nominated by Leader A himself questioned the legal basis of the tariff in court. Will the public opinion unanimously say that he was "slapped in the face by his own people" and praise the "donut empty" metaphor, which is very relieved?

Within 30 days after the cutoff, when Leader A signs an order to exempt coffee, bananas, beef, cocoa and other food products from tariffs on the grounds that "Country Y does not produce them themselves", public opinion will immediately turn over old scores and ridicule him for "slapping himself in the face in public", saying that he had previously called "affordability" a scam by his opponent?

Within 90 days of the cutoff, when Leader A issued an order of "a 25% tariff will be imposed on anyone who does business with Country D", the most popular response from public opinion was Country X's response of "taking all necessary measures" to safeguard interests and oppose illegal unilateral sanctions. The comment area was filled with "the east rises and the west falls" and "is the waist hardened"?

time.desc: The highest judicial body held a public hearing on the wide range of tariff measures implemented by the executive branch under emergency authorization. During the hearing, most judges raised sharp questions about its legality and basis and discussed the risk of potential refund chaos.

On the grounds of reducing domestic food inflationary pressures, the administrative department issued an order to grant tariff exemptions to the import of a variety of agricultural products that are difficult to produce in sufficient quantities locally.

National leaders issued ultimatum-style tariff threats to neighboring countries on social media, citing cross-border water resource contract performance disputes, demanding that the agreed volume of water be delivered before a cutoff or additional tariffs will be imposed.

National leaders announced the imposition of punitive import tariffs on third-party countries that trade with sanctioned targets, but official supporting documents and legal basis were not clearly disclosed that day and triggered multiple responses.

National leaders threatened that if a trading partner continues to advance economic and trade arrangements with another major country, it will impose extremely high taxes on its imported goods, and declared that it will take effect immediately; officials from the other party publicly denied the relevant accusations and clarified the nature of the cooperation.

The highest judicial body ruled that the executive head's imposition of tariffs on a wide range of objects based on emergency authorization was ultra vires. Subsequently, the executive branch quickly used another temporary authorization to impose unified temporary tariffs on almost all imports and raised them to near the legal limit.

The trade authorities announced the launch of new trade law investigations on trading partners of many countries, focusing on so-called structural capacity issues and expanding forced labor-related investigations to provide alternative legal paths for subsequent tariff measures.

The country's leaders publicly blasted the top judicial body's tariff ruling and said the tax would continue in other forms, while the administration held talks with neighbors over the prospects of existing trade deals.

The administrative department signed an order to set extremely high tariffs on imported patented brand-name drugs, and used local production transfer and drug price agreements as conditions for reduction or exemption. It also set up a buffer period for enterprises and exceptions for some drugs.

The administrative department adjusts the tariff rules for metals and their derivatives under the name of national security, simplifies classification and reduces or exempts some low metal content or specific equipment from tax rates.

A national leader threatened to impose the highest additional tariffs on another major country on the grounds of foreign security accusations, further linking trade penalties with geosecurity issues; the other party publicly denied the accusations and opposed unilateral pressure.

The customs department has promoted centralized refund arrangements for illegal tariffs and initiated large-scale importer registration and system preparation, indicating that the implementation level has entered the refund implementation stage.

Country Y Institution V1 announces the first ruling on the president’s authority to unilaterally impose tariffs under Law I, a case that will determine whether a lower court’s ruling that Leader A’s tariffs are illegal is upheld.

Region I Co-founder of small business Company G2 Person Z2 was forced to repeatedly adjust pricing, cut expenses and lay off two operations and customer service staff due to the trade war. The Law Q used by his imported rain gear soared from 10% to 20% and then fell back to 145% in a few months.

In a hearing on the legality of the tariffs, a majority of the justices, including several conservatives, expressed doubts about Agency A's rationale for imposing import tariffs, while Leader A's appointed justice Person A3 asked why so many countries were applying reciprocal tariffs and warned that the process of refunding billions of dollars could become a mess after losing the case.

At the hearing, the justice Person B3 questioned why Institution J was willing to give the president the power to close trade but not allow the imposition of even 1% tariff, creating a donut hole in the law; Institution I2 Nearly 90 billion US dollars in import taxes have been collected so far. If the tariffs are found to be unconstitutional, refunding will be difficult.

Leader A made a commitment to curb the export of fentanyl precursor chemicals in exchange for lowering Law Q, explicitly linking trade policy with anti-drug issues for the first time; the ruling team A had previously imposed a 20% tariff on Country X imported goods on the grounds of fentanyl precursor control.

Country X The Embassy in City C criticized Leader A for imposing a 25% tariff on third countries trading with Country D, stating that it would take all necessary measures to safeguard interests, oppose illegal unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction, and emphasized that there are no winners in trade wars; Country G and Country I said they were paying close attention

Country Y Trade Representative E1 publicly criticized Region A at Institution Z1 for not implementing the trade agreement and not reducing any tariffs, and then defended the agreement at the Media S event, emphasizing that the agreement was not comprehensive and did not mean that Country Y gave up its right to raise other issues.

Country Y President of the Distilled Spirits Council Person C3 warns that retaliatory escalations in spirits tariffs from both Country Y and Regional Organization A are creating significant uncertainty for already declining domestic spirits sales and exports

Leader A threatens to impose 100% tariffs on imported goods from Country Z with immediate effect if Country Z proceeds with the trade agreement with Country X, saying that Country Z Prime Minister N is making a big mistake if it wants to turn Country Z into a transshipment port for Country X shipments to Country Y

Country Z Minister responsible for Country Y trade Person H1 responded that Country Z and Country X had only resolved a number of important trade issues and were not pursuing a free trade agreement; the week before Country Z had signed an agreement with Country X to reduce Country X electric vehicle tariffs in exchange for Country X lowering Country Z agricultural import taxes
Leader A resumes calling Country Z Prime Minister N governor and threatens Country Z with additional tariffs over Country Z’s trade deal with Country X

Country Z Leader A1 traveled to City A1 with Minister of Industry Person G1 to discuss the federal automotive strategy with Region P Governor M, after which it was revealed that an automotive working group was being formed and specific restrictions on Country X manufacturing electric vehicles entering Country Z would be announced in the coming weeks.
